title: Coordinate multi-index partial derivative on real Euclidean space
statement: Use the fields $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. For $m\geq0$, $\alpha:\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\to\mathbf N$ and any function $f:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf C$, define $\partial^\alpha f$ by applying $\partial_j g(x)=D_{\mathbf R}g(x)(e_j)$ exactly $\alpha_j$ times in each standard coordinate, composing these operators in increasing coordinate order, with coordinate $0$ outermost. Here $D_{\mathbf R}$ is the real Frechet derivative, taken as zero at a point where the function is not differentiable, as in Mathlib fderiv. More explicitly, concatenate the lists containing $\alpha_j$ copies of $j$ for $j=0,\ldots,m-1$, and right-fold $g\mapsto(x\mapsto D_{\mathbf R}g(x)(e_j))$ over this list, starting from $f$. In particular $\partial^0f=f$, including $m=0$. On a smooth function these are the usual commuting mixed coordinate partial derivatives.

source.place: Supplemental Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 1 (1.1), p.1: coordinate multi-index derivative convention; existing implementation extracted from the Plancherel weak-derivative module at maintainer request.
